note: Authored by reading Tafsir al-Tabari in English against the reader's modern translation. Each phrase carries the app's own words for that piece of the verse, a plain modern English line of my own, the Arabic of the piece, and the numbered paragraphs of the commentary that speak of it.

phrases.translation: When the sky bursts open
phrases.text: When the heaven tears and breaks apart, so that it becomes gates.

phrases.translation: obeying its Lord as it must
phrases.text: The heavens listened to their Lord as they burst apart, and obeyed Him in what He commanded them. The Arabic word means to listen and to obey, and the saying was made obligatory upon them.

phrases.translation: and when the earth is flattened out
phrases.text: And when the earth is levelled flat and enlarged in its expanse. The Prophet said that on the day of resurrection the earth will be spread out until there is room for no more than the space of a man's two feet.

phrases.translation: and ejects ˹all˺ its contents
phrases.text: The earth casts out onto its surface what was inside it of the dead.

phrases.translation: and becomes empty
phrases.text: And it empties itself of them unto God. Some read it as bringing out its burdens and all that was inside it.

phrases.translation: obeying its Lord as it must,
phrases.text: And the earth listened to the command of its Lord in casting out the dead onto its surface, and God made it obligatory upon it to obey.

phrases.translation: ˹surely you will all be judged˺
phrases.text: The grammarians differed about where the answer to the opening clause falls. Tabari holds that it is left out, and that the meaning is: when the heaven is split asunder, man sees the good or the evil he has sent forward.

phrases.translation: O humanity! Indeed, you are labouring restlessly towards your Lord, and will ˹eventually˺ meet the consequences
phrases.text: O man, you are working hard towards your Lord, and you will meet Him with that work, whether it be good or evil. So let the work be something that carries you away from His displeasure and brings you His good pleasure. Qatada says your labour is feeble, so put it into obedience to God if you can.
phrases.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَدۡحٗا فَمُلَٰقِيهِ

phrases.translation: As for those who are given their record in their right hand
phrases.text: As for the one who is given the book of his deeds in his right hand.

phrases.translation: they will have an easy reckoning
phrases.text: His deeds will be examined, and the evil in them forgiven and the good rewarded. The Prophet used to say: O God, reckon with me with an easy reckoning. Ibn Zayd explains it as the sins being forgiven and the good deeds accepted, and says it is the reckoning for which remission is granted.

phrases.translation: and will return to their people joyfully
phrases.text: He will go back rejoicing to his family in the Garden, to a family for whom God has prepared Paradise.

phrases.translation: And as for those who are given their record ˹in their left hand˺ from behind their backs
phrases.text: As for the one whose book is given behind his back. That is because his right hand is drawn up to his neck and his left hand is put behind his back, so that he takes the book with the left hand from behind him.
phrases.ar: وَأَمَّا مَنۡ أُوتِيَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ وَرَآءَ ظَهۡرِهِۦ

phrases.translation: they will cry for ˹instant˺ destruction
phrases.text: He will cry out for annihilation, that is, woe to me and woe to my destruction. The commentators say the same thing.

phrases.translation: and will burn in the blazing Fire
phrases.text: He will burn in a searing fire. The reciters differ on the reading: some read it as God making them burn over and over, one roasting after another, and some as their burning in it. Tabari says both readings are well known and the reciter is right either way.

phrases.translation: For they used to be prideful among their people
phrases.text: In this world he was proud and pleased with himself among his people, because of what was in him of disobedience to God.

phrases.translation: thinking they would never return ˹to Allah˺
phrases.text: He thought in this world that he would never return to God and would not be raised again after death, so he did not concern himself with his sins, expecting no reward and fearing no punishment.

phrases.translation: Yes ˹they would˺!
phrases.text: Yes indeed, he will surely return and come back to his Lord, alive as he was before his death.

phrases.translation: Surely their Lord has always been All-Seeing of them
phrases.text: The Lord of this one who thought he would not return was watching him all along in this world, both in the sins he committed and in what his affair would come to. He knows all of it.

phrases.translation: So, I do swear by the twilight
phrases.text: God swears by the twilight glow. The commentators differed: some said it is the red glow on the western horizon after sunset, others that it is the day itself. Tabari holds that He swore by the day as it retreats and by the night as it comes on.

phrases.translation: And by the night and whatever it envelops
phrases.text: God swears by the night and by what it gathers in. The commentators say it gathers the living creatures that come to rest in it, the things that fly and crawl by day, and they say it drives the darkness onward and everything to its place of refuge. The word also means a great quantity of provisions gathered together.

phrases.translation: And by the moon when it waxes full
phrases.text: God swears by the moon when it is full, that is, when it is complete and evenly round. Some say it means the thirteenth night of the month, when the moon has gathered itself together.

phrases.translation: You will certainly pass from one state to another
phrases.text: You will pass from one state to another, and from one matter to another, through the heavy trials. The commentators differed: some took it of the Prophet alone, some of the heavens one above the other, some of the hereafter after this life, and some of the sky changing colour. Tabari keeps it general.

phrases.translation: So what is the matter with them that they do not believe
phrases.text: What is it with these people that they do not hold God to be one and do not acknowledge the resurrection, when their Lord has sworn to them that they will pass through state after state, and they have already seen the proofs of his oneness?

phrases.translation: and when the Quran is recited to them, they do not bow down ˹in submission˺
phrases.text: And when the Book of their Lord is recited to them, they do not submit themselves and do not bow down humbly.
phrases.ar: وَإِذَا قُرِئَ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ لَا يَسۡجُدُونَۤ۩

phrases.translation: In fact, the disbelievers persist in denial
phrases.text: Nay, those who disbelieve deny the signs of God and his revelation.

phrases.translation: But Allah knows best whatever they hide
phrases.text: God knows best what these people keep in their breasts, and the hearts are the storehouse of deeds, the good and the evil alike. He knows what they hide and what they publish.

phrases.translation: So give them good news of a painful punishment
phrases.text: Announce to them, O Muhammad, a punishment that awaits them with God, and that is agonizing for them.

phrases.translation: But those who believe and do good will have a never-ending reward
phrases.text: Those who believed and did the good have a reward that is neither counted nor diminished. To have believed is to have repented, to have held God to be one, and to have acknowledged the prophethood of Muhammad and the resurrection. To have done the good is to have done what God required and left what He forbade.
phrases.ar: إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ لَهُمۡ أَجۡرٌ غَيۡرُ مَمۡنُونِۭ
